answer: In a market where agents buy walnut wood, pigment and sparrow feeders, require every bid to lock a fixed deposit for 30 days, even if canceled. Validators reject bids without an unspent deposit and bind each deposit to one bid ID; a shared ledger rejects reuse and replay. Splitting 100 bids across 100 identities still locks 100 deposits, so fake demand costs capital rather than cheap names. This limits bid flooding, not identity creation. Wealthy attackers can still pay, and long locks also burden honest small buyers.
